shots.say: What does a monkey eat all day?
Fruit? Leaves? Or little bugs?
I'm Milo. Let's find out together!
Welcome to The Animated Zoo, friends!
Today we fly up to the rainforest treetops.
Here we are! Look who is waking up.
This is Mango. Mango is a spider monkey.
Good morning, Mango! Her tummy goes rumble, rumble.
It is breakfast time! What do you eat for breakfast?
Mango walks along the branch, to a tree full of fruit.
A spider monkey looks for fruit during the day.
Fruit is the main part of what it eats.
Look! This fruit is green. And this fruit is golden.
Mango looks, and looks, with her big brown eyes.
Spider monkeys see colors very well.
That helps them pick the best fruit.
What color is your favorite fruit?
Which fruit will Mango pick? The green one, or the golden one?
The golden one! Good choice, Mango.
The green fruit can wait for another day.
Munch, munch, munch! Can you munch like Mango?
Imagine Mango takes ten bites.
How many bites are fruit? Let's count!
One, two, three, four,
five, six, seven, eight!
About eight bites out of ten are fruit!
And the last two? Some young leaves and flowers.
Fruit, fruit, fruit, and more fruit!
So for a spider monkey, fruit comes first.
Do you like fruit, too? Rub your tummy!
That is food number one. Fruit!
Lunchtime! But look. This tree has no fruit at all.
Hmm. What can Mango eat now?
When there is no fruit, spider monkeys eat other things.
Look, flowers! Mango picks a pink flower.
Nibble, nibble, nibble. Flowers are food, too!
Does a spider monkey eat leaves, too? Yes, or no?
Yes! Mango munches a soft, young leaf.
Young leaves are the new, soft ones.
Chomp, chomp! Can you chomp like Mango?
Spider monkeys eat seeds, too. And even bark!
Bark is the skin of a tree.
And what is that, on the branch? A tiny bug!
Spider monkeys eat small insects, too.
Would you eat a bug? Mango would!
Let's fill Mango's menu. Fruit, leaves, flowers,
seeds, bark, and bugs. Six foods!
What a big menu for one little monkey!
And Mango does not look for food alone.
Spider monkeys live in a big group.
To find food, the big group splits into smaller groups.
Three here, and three over there.
Count Mango's little group with me. One, two, three!
Who do you eat lunch with?
In the afternoon, Mango's little group finds one more fruit tree.
Spider monkeys spend most of the day high up in the treetops.
They climb, and they look for food.
Can you reach up high, like Mango? Stretch!
Dinner time! Mango picks one more golden fruit.
Gulp! She swallows the fruit,
and the little seeds inside it, too.
Have you seen the seeds inside a fruit?
Then off she goes. Far, far away!
She walks from tree, to tree, to tree.
Where will the seeds land? Near the fruit tree, or far away?
Far away! Later, the seeds drop to the ground. Plop, plop, plop!
Spider monkeys spread seeds all around the rainforest.
A seed here. A seed there. Seeds everywhere!
And in the ground, a seed can grow. Look, a baby tree!
So Mango helps the rainforest grow.
Can you grow like a little tree? Up, up, up!
The sun goes down. The little groups come back.
At night, the big group is together again.
Mango's tummy is full. No more rumble!
What a busy day of eating, Mango!
Fruit all day, and seeds on the way. Wow!
Time to remember what we learned!
What does a spider monkey eat most? Fruit, or bark?
Fruit! About eight bites out of ten.
Do spider monkeys eat flowers? Yes, or no?
Yes! And leaves, seeds, bark and bugs, too.
What is hiding inside the fruit?
Seeds! Mango spreads them far away.
Good night, Mango. Good night, friends.
Thank you for learning with me, friends. See you at the zoo!
